question: With one unit selected, what does a click on the map's pictures answer - and with a unit selected that has no counter on the map?

addresses.name: ProvinceGraphics_HitTest
addresses.revises: comment only: what keeps sel (its avatar under the mouse, or no avatar at all), what the walk gathers with sel and what the end answers when sel is not among them, read off the bytes
addresses.signature: void* __stdcall ProvinceGraphics_HitTest(void* owner, void* provinceGraphics, float* mouse, CList* selection)
addresses.comment: **What a click on a province's pictures picks** (MapGraphics_PickUnderPointer asks it after the battles). Each picture is asked by its 3D object's slot 20 for a ray from the mouse through the camera's projection, and **kept only where its score is strictly above the best so far** (`jbe` at 0x64109F against nought, 0x64111B, 0x6412FA), the best starting at nought: a building or large base picture scores 1.0 (CBillboardObject::HitTest), a counter `(order + 1) * 0.1 + 1` (CCounterObject::HitTest), so **a counter over a building picture always wins**. The large air base picture (+0x7C) offers the air base's selectable (CMapProvince +0x54, +0x18; kind 8), the large naval base picture (+0x80) the CPort (+0x354; kind 4). **sel**: where exactly one thing is selected, of kind 0, 1 or 2, and its own avatar (+0x164) is under the mouse - **or it has no avatar at all** (0x64117F), which is a fleet in port and an air unit at its own base. With the camera at 500 or under, each 3D object of the province (+0x10, +0xDC, next +0xD8) scoring above the best so far: where the counters are on (settings word bit 0x800), the province's unit vector (+0x2C8) at its cursor (+0x2E8) is asked - with the camera above counter_distance and that unit not selected and not at its own base, it alone (intel 2 or more) is taken where this object is its avatar; otherwise the vector is walked round from the cursor, and **with sel every unit the player knows at 2 or more, in sel's province (+0x130), of sel's owner (+0x128) and not at its own base is gathered in that order**, the last whose object is shown kept at [ebp-0x34], and the walk stops; without sel the unit whose avatar this object is wins. Then, **only without sel** (0x641479), where the buildings are on (bit 0x20), the object shown and the province not hidden by fog, a building picture (+0x40 vector) offers the CPort for a naval base, the air base's selectable for an air base, the building (kind 6) otherwise. **With sel the answer is the unit after sel in what was gathered, wrapping** (0x64157C) - so clicking the one selected unit's counter again picks the next of its owner's units in the province - **and where sel is not among them, the last unit gathered, or 0**: so with a unit selected that has no counter, a click finds no building picture and a counter only of its owner's units in its own province, and otherwise answers 0, the caller falling to the province. Otherwise the best hit, or 0. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 2026-11-13: the sel set-up 0x641133..0x6411DA (the avatar-less exit at 0x64117F leaves [ebp-0x18] set), the near walk 0x6413C8..0x641473 (province +0x130 and owner +0x128 compared, 0x5CDC30 excluding a unit at its base, 0x6434C0 appending, [ebp-0x34] written at 0x64144B), and the end 0x64157C..0x641666 (the search for sel, `(i + 1) mod count` at 0x64160B, [ebp-0x34] returned at 0x6415F2). Wrong if 0x5CDC30 is not 'at its own base' - its name is the selection reading's - or if MapGraphics_PickUnderPointer does not fall to the province on 0 (the selection reading's order).

frontier: 0x5CDC30 - taken here, as in the selection reading, to answer whether a unit is at its own base; not read for this
